evidence: src/shared/base.controller.ts: `getUserIdFromToken(authorization)` splits the Authorization header (`authorization.split(' ')[1]`) and calls `jwt.verify(token, SECRET)`, which is request authentication and therefore a presentation/transport concern.
src/shared/base.controller.ts: there are no repository or database calls and no business rules; the class only holds a protected helper for subclass controllers.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/shared/base.controller.ts is a presentation-layer base controller. Its only responsibility is `getUserIdFromToken`, which reads the HTTP Authorization header, takes the bearer token, checks it with jwt.verify and returns the user id. Reading request credentials is a transport/HTTP concern. In this layer model, guards (src/common/guards/**, **/*.guard.ts) are presentation, so handling authentication at this layer fits its role. The file has no business rules, no persistence and no domain logic. One could argue that verifying the token signature belongs in an infrastructure strategy (**/strategies/**). However, a controller decoding the caller's identity from the request is a common presentation responsibility, not a clear move into another layer kind. No ADR prose contradicts this.
